title: Your Endpoint Management Platform Could Be Your Biggest Security Risk
content_md: Endpoint management platforms have become essential in modern IT operations and enterprise security. They allow administrators to deploy patches, install software, execute scripts, enforce configurations, and remotely manage thousands of devices from a centralized system. Without these types of systems, maintaining consistent security across large environments would be extremely difficult and labor-intensive. However, the administrative authority that makes these platforms valuable also makes them very attractive targets for attackers. An endpoint management platform already has established and approved communication channels, elevated permissions, and trusted relationships with the devices it manages. Any attacker who gains control of that infrastructure will be able to use those existing capabilities to distribute malware, execute malicious commands, disable security controls, or disrupt operations across an entire organization. All with the same level of authority as the real admin. The same capabilities that allow an administrator to secure thousands of endpoints can allow an attacker to compromise them. Recent incidents demonstrate how compromised remote management infrastructure can extend attacks across compromised environments. In 2026, Huntress documented attackers abusing compromised BeyondTrust Bomgar remote support infrastructure to deploy ransomware and access downstream organizations.
